overview: The Medford Zoning Board of Appeals (ZBA) adjudicates petitions for variances, special permits, and findings, alongside administrative appeals of the Building Commissioner's decisions. Meeting from early 2023 through late 2026, the board focuses on residential expansions, commercial redevelopments, and large-scale multifamily projects under Massachusetts General Law Chapter 40B. The ZBA manages local density by reviewing conversions of single-family homes and evaluating site-specific hardships. At the most recent meeting, the board was navigating new state regulations regarding Accessory Dwelling Units while continuing to manage residential use variances and special permits.

threads.name: 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway 40B Development
threads.summary: The board conducted an extensive review of a 350-unit residential development, focusing on fire safety for wood-frame construction and peer reviews of traffic and design. Early sessions addressed pedestrian access to Wellington Station and the implementation of a 70% local preference policy for affordable units. The board approved the comprehensive permit in July 2023 with conditions including a partial linkage fee waiver of $758,000 and the establishment of a phased occupancy plan. In late 2024, the board determined that refinements to bike storage, trash rooms, and rooftop amenities were insubstantial changes that did not require a new permit.

threads.name: 970 Fellsway 40B Development
threads.summary: A 289-unit multifamily development at 970 Fellsway underwent months of review concerning traffic impacts and building massing on Amaranth Avenue. The board requested design revisions to include building height step-downs and increased setbacks to better integrate the project with neighboring residential properties. Following discussions on linkage fees and off-site infrastructure improvements, the board approved the comprehensive permit and a partial fee waiver of $816,564. Subsequent approvals allowed a lot split to separate the residential development from an existing nonconforming storage building on the site.

threads.name: Cannabis Dispensary Operations
threads.summary: The board oversaw the incremental expansion of services for a retail marijuana dispensary at 114 Mystic Avenue. Initial approvals focused on site security and traffic safety for retail sales at the former VFW hall. Over several years, the board granted additional special permits to allow medical cannabis sales, product manufacturing, and eventually courier delivery services. Each expansion was conditioned on consultations with the police chief and adherence to city safety protocols.

threads.name: Residential Density and Conversions
threads.summary: The board frequently reviews petitions to convert single-family dwellings into two-family or multi-family residences. Successful petitions often demonstrate a lack of substantial detriment to the neighborhood, such as the three-family conversion at 12 George Street or the conversion of a commercial unit to residential on Main Street. However, the board denied some requests, such as a garage conversion at 52 Garfield Avenue, due to concerns over setting precedents for principal structures in single-family zones. Recent approvals for lot area variances continue to facilitate density increases on undersized lots.

threads.name: Fence Height and Boundary Relief
threads.summary: Property owners regularly seek variances for fences exceeding the standard six-foot height limit, often citing unique topography or security needs. The board has approved 10-foot fences for the Housing Authority and industrial sites, and 8-foot fences for residential privacy in cases of significant elevation differences. Conversely, the board denied a fence variance on Winford Way after neighbors testified it created a 'prison wall' effect. Recent approvals for fences on corner lots have been conditioned on maintaining visibility at intersections for traffic safety.

threads.name: Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs)
threads.summary: In late 2026, the board began evaluating petitions for Accessory Dwelling Units under updated state zoning regulations. Proposed projects on Vassar Street and Wellesley Street involving attic expansions and shed dormers have been continued to allow for legal counsel review. The board is seeking to align local decisions with new state guidelines while addressing concerns about building massing and protected ADU status.

threads.name: Administrative Appeals and Enforcement
threads.summary: The board hears appeals from residents regarding zoning enforcement actions taken by the Building Commissioner. In one notable case on Waterville Road, the board upheld a notice of violation against a property owner for operating a commercial gutter business in a residential zone. This decision followed testimony from neighbors regarding noise and idling trucks, reinforcing the prohibition of commercial operations in single-family districts.

citations.title: 91 Waterville Road: Administrative Appeal of Notice of Violation
citations.label: M57#1

periods.narrative: This period was dominated by the technical review and final approval of the 350-unit Chapter 40B development at 4000 Mystic Valley Parkway.
The board processed the 970 Fellsway 40B permit and underwent significant leadership changes including the election of multiple new chairs.
Work shifted toward interpreting new state mandates for Accessory Dwelling Units and adjudicating administrative appeals of residential zoning violations.
